where: Section 3 (bulletin 'TDC reference and pegging', last line) and Exam traps (trap 1)
problem: It says a wrong peg leaves 'every imep ... wrong by a constant' and that 'a missing peg moves both peak pressure and imep'. A constant pressure offset cancels in the closed-cycle integral ∮p dV, because the cycle starts and ends at the same volume, so imep is almost unaffected by a pegging error. What a wrong peg really corrupts is the absolute level: peak pressure, the pressure trace in bar, polytropic index and the heat-release rate curve. Only the angle error (TDC offset), not the pressure offset, distorts imep, and only slightly.
fix: Without pegging the trace floats at the wrong absolute level: peak pressure and the heat-release curve are wrong, but the imep taken as ∮p dV over the closed cycle is largely unaffected because a constant offset cancels in the integral. A TDC (angle) error does move imep, but only slightly.

problem: Written as 'pVn = constant'; the exponent is not a superscript. Quiz Q2 writes 'pV^n', so the notation is inconsistent, and a student may read pVn as p × V × n.
fix: Write pVⁿ = constant (or pV^n in the same style everywhere).

problem: 'Cylinder pressure swings from about 1 bar to 80 bar' is only true for spark-ignition engines. A turbocharged diesel peaks near 150–180 bar, which this chapter also covers (imep, pegging and heat release are shown for diesels too).
fix: Range the sentence: in a spark-ignition engine roughly 1 bar to 80 bar; in a turbocharged diesel the peak can reach about 150 bar or more.

problem: 'It is the cycle behind the BS VI limits' is too broad. BS VI type approval for cars and light-duty vehicles uses MIDC, but BS VI for two-wheelers uses the WMTC.
fix: Say MIDC is the type-approval cycle for BS VI cars and light-duty vehicles; two-wheelers are certified on WMTC.
